what: Why splines, and why they are awkward here
title: Restricted cubic splines for complex survey data
text: Real exposure–outcome relationships rarely straight lines. usual workarounds cost something: categorising continuous exposure throws away information power, assuming linearity misspecifies model, polynomials behave badly extremes. Restricted cubic splines fit smooth curve constrained linear beyond outer knots, keeps tails stable leaving middle flexible. Complex surveys NHANES make awkward. Valid analysis needs three design features: sampling weights, without point estimates biased population, clustering stratification, without standard errors — therefore every confidence interval p-value — wrong. rms, natural home restricted cubic splines R, know . survey handles three spline helper. svyrcs bridge: spline fitted inside survey model, estimates use weights confidence band uses variance estimator design implies: Taylor linearisation ordinary survey.design, replicate-weight variance svyrep.design.

what: Does the curve differ by subgroup?
title: Restricted cubic splines for complex survey data
text: Cross spline grouping variable svyrcs() fits one model, returning curve per group:  Two questions get separate answers. Interaction asks whether association differs groups . Shape interaction drops linear interaction term, asks narrower question: curvature differ, one curve simply shifted copy ? neither close significant, worth dwelling . two curves figure look different — minimum sits couple BMI units higher women, male curve climbs sooner — 31 design degrees freedom separation well inside noise. Reporting “association stronger men” fit supported. Subgroup curves easy -read, exactly interaction p-value printed next . facet = TRUE gives group panel bands overlap much read:  details worth knowing: One model, several. Covariate effects — age — shared across groups. Fitting subgroup separately estimate independently produce interaction test . groups share one reference value, curves comparable. ref = "min" reference minimum-risk point reference level, output names . standard error non-reference group accounts covariance main interaction coefficients. Adding two variances separately, obvious shortcut, gives wrong interval. modifier must factor, character logical. Continuous effect modification supported. predict(fit, x = ..., group = "Female") gives numbers one group.

code: library(svyrcs) library(survey) library(survival)  design <- svydesign(   id = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~weight,   nest = TRUE, data = nhanes_bmi )  fit <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + sex + race, design = design) fit #> Restricted cubic spline on a complex survey design #> #>   Model      survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards #>   Outcome    Surv(time, event) #>   Exposure   bmi, 4 knots at 19.78, 25.22, 29.71, 40.67 (weighted quantiles) #>   Sample     10,617 observations, 1,893 events, 31 design df #>   Reference  bmi = 27.35 (weighted median), HR = 1 #> #>   Overall association  F = 43.58 on 3 and 31 df,  p = 3.12e-11 #>   Non-linearity        F = 51.70 on 2 and 31 df,  p = 1.34e-10  plot(fit)                          # curve with confidence band (ggplot2 if installed) summary(fit)                       # turning points, where the band excludes the null predict(fit, x = c(25, 30, 35))    # estimates at values you choose svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age, design = design, ref = "min") by_sex <- svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) * sex + age, design = design) by_sex$tests$interaction   # p for interaction by_sex$tests$shape         # does the *curvature* differ, or is the curve just shifted? plot(by_sex)               # one coloured curve per group; facet = TRUE to panel them design_mi <- svydesign(id = ~psu, strata = ~strata, weights = ~weight,                        nest = TRUE, data = mitools::imputationList(completed_datasets)) svyrcs(Surv(time, event) ~ rcs(bmi, 4) + age + tchol, design = design_mi)

text: First release. svyrcs() fits restricted cubic spline model complex survey design returns exposure-response curve, tests reference value single object. Survey-weighted Cox (svycoxph) generalised linear (svyglm) models supported, giving hazard ratios, odds ratios, rate ratios mean differences. rcs() builds restricted cubic spline basis use inside model formula. Knots stored basis reused predict() makepredictcall() method, predictions can never made silently re-derived knots. basis numerically identical rms::rcs(). svyrcs_curve() estimates curve already-fitted survey model. Curves estimated contrasts reference value, covariates cancel exactly covariate reference grid needed. Confidence intervals use t quantile survey degrees freedom survey::degf(). Reference values may given directly chosen survey-weighted median, mean arbitrary weighted quantile, minimum- maximum-risk point curve. Tests overall association non-linearity reported design-based F tests (matching survey::regTermTest()) alongside chi-square form. print(), summary(), plot(), autoplot() predict() methods. nhanes_bmi, public-domain NHANES extract linked mortality follow-, examples tests.
